title: Complaint: ID blocked or account deactivated
summary: Ask the platform in writing for the exact reason and a chance to appeal. Keep every message. Escalate step by step if there is no answer.
steps: Write to the platform's support in the app and ask for the exact reason and how to appeal. Keep the ticket number
Email the platform's grievance officer. Most platforms publish this contact on their website or in the app under Contact or Policies
If there is no reply in about 15 days (a sensible wait, not a legal limit), complain to your state labour department
Call the e-Shram helpline 14434 and ask where to complain about a platform in your state
If your state has a gig-worker law (Rajasthan, Karnataka, Bihar, Jharkhand, Telangana), ask the labour department about its complaint process
For serious harm, ask for free legal aid on 15100
documents_needed: Screenshot of the block message
Your worker ID and registered phone number
Screenshots of recent ratings and earnings
Ticket numbers and dates of your messages to support
status_note: Which authority takes platform complaints, and what notice a platform must give before deactivation, depends on your state and the platform's policy. The wait times here are suggestions, not legal deadlines. Never promise reinstatement.

title: Complaint: payment short or missing
summary: If a platform paid less than the app showed, or has not paid at all, collect the trips and amounts, ask support for a written breakdown, and escalate if it is not fixed.
steps: List the dates, trip or order IDs and the amount the app showed against the amount you received
Raise a ticket in the app and ask for a written breakdown of the difference. Keep the ticket number
Email the platform's grievance officer with the list and screenshots
If it stays unpaid after about 15 days (a sensible wait, not a legal limit), complain to the state labour department
Call 14434 for guidance on where to complain in your state
documents_needed: Screenshots of the earnings screen showing the amount due
Bank statement or SMS showing what was received
Trip or order IDs and dates
Ticket numbers

title: Complaint: wrongful penalty or deduction
summary: If money was cut as a penalty, fine or fee that you think is wrong, ask for the exact rule and the proof, and ask for a review in writing.
steps: Note the date, amount and the reason the app gave. Take a screenshot
Ask support in writing which rule was applied and what proof they have. Keep the ticket number
Ask for a review of the penalty and for the money to be returned if it is wrong
Email the platform's grievance officer if support does not fix it
If there is no answer in about 15 days (a sensible wait, not a legal limit), complain to the state labour department
documents_needed: Screenshot of the penalty or deduction
Screenshots of the order, chat or customer complaint if you have them
Your earnings screen before and after
Ticket numbers

title: Complaint: promised incentive or bonus not paid
summary: If you completed an offer's target but the bonus was not paid, show the offer terms and your numbers and ask for the payment in writing.
steps: Take a screenshot of the offer and its terms, and of your completed trips or orders
Raise a ticket and ask for the incentive to be paid or for a written reason it was not. Keep the ticket number
Email the platform's grievance officer with the offer screenshot and your count
If it stays unpaid after about 15 days (a sensible wait, not a legal limit), complain to the state labour department
documents_needed: Screenshot of the offer terms and dates
Screenshot of your completed count
Earnings statement for those days
Ticket numbers

title: Complaint: accident help or insurance claim refused or delayed
summary: After an accident, keep all medical papers and report it in the platform app. If the platform's accident cover is refused or delayed, write to the platform and the insurer, and check any personal accident insurance you hold.
steps: Report the accident in the platform app right away and note the report number
Keep hospital bills, discharge papers, photos and the police report or FIR copy if one was made
Ask the platform in writing how to claim its accident cover and by when. Keep the reply
If you have PMSBY or another personal accident insurance, ask your bank how to claim and by when
If the claim is refused or delayed, email the platform's grievance officer and the insurer's grievance contact
Call 14434 for guidance, and 15100 for free legal aid if the claim is large or refused
documents_needed: Hospital bills and discharge summary
Police report or FIR copy if made
Photos of the accident and injuries
Platform accident report number
Insurance policy details if you have any
status_note: What accident cover a platform provides, and how to claim it, differs by platform. Do not promise that any cover applies. Claim deadlines vary, so ask early.

title: Complaint: harassment, abuse or threats
summary: Your safety comes first. If you are in danger call 112. Report abuse to the platform's safety team, keep evidence, and women can also reach the women helpline and the district Local Committee.
steps: If you are in danger now, call 112. Women can also call 181
Report it in the platform app and ask for the safety team. Keep the report number
Save screenshots, call logs, chats and the order details. Do not delete anything
For serious threats or assault, a police complaint is your right. Ask for a copy of the complaint (FIR or receipt)
Women can also approach the Local Committee for sexual harassment set up by the District Officer. Ask at the district collector's office
Call 15100 for free legal aid
documents_needed: Screenshots of messages and call logs
Order or trip details with date and time
Names or description of the person if known
Witness names if any
status_note: How a platform handles safety reports, and whether the district Local Committee covers a particular platform job, can differ. Always start with 112 when in danger.

title: Complaint: wages not paid by a contractor or employer
summary: For daily-wage and contract work, write down the days worked and the agreed rate, ask for payment, and complain to the labour department if it is still unpaid.
steps: Write down the dates you worked, the agreed daily rate and what you were paid
Ask the contractor or employer for the amount due. Do it with a witness or by message so there is a record
Take photos of attendance sheets, messages and any payment proof
If it stays unpaid, complain to the state labour department or the Labour Commissioner's office in your district
Construction workers can also ask the state construction workers' welfare board for help
Call 15100 for free legal aid
documents_needed: Dates worked and agreed rate
Name and phone of the contractor or employer and the site address
Photos of attendance or work records
Messages about payment
Names of co-workers who can confirm
status_note: The office that handles wage complaints, and its process, depends on the state. Confirm where to go with the state labour department.

title: Complaint: wrong traffic challan
summary: If a challan is wrong, check it on the official e-challan portal, collect your proof, and contest it online or in the traffic court. Pay only through official channels.
steps: Check the challan on the official e-challan portal using your vehicle number
Collect proof that it is wrong: photos, the place and time, your documents, GPS or trip records
Contest it on the portal or in the traffic court named on the challan
If it is correct and you choose to pay, pay only on the official portal or at an official counter and keep the receipt
documents_needed: Challan number and vehicle number
Vehicle registration, licence and insurance
Photos or trip records that show where you were
Receipt if already paid
